text: Managing a team effectively requires a balance of several key skills. First, clear communication is essential, as it ensures everyone understands their roles and the team’s goals. A good leader also practices delegation, trusting team members with specific tasks rather than doing everything alone. This not only reduces pressure on the leader but also helps others grow. Regular feedback is equally important; it should be constructive, pointing out what works and what can be improved. Motivation keeps energy high, whether through recognition or offering support. Finally, when conflicts arise, addressing them quickly and fairly is crucial. By listening to both sides and finding a common solution, a manager can turn a disagreement into a chance for stronger cooperation.
